$\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(\mathbf{x}) e^{-i 2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}\cdot\mathbf{x}}\, d\mathbf{x}$		 $\widehat{f}_2(\boldsymbol{\omega}) \triangleq$
$\dfrac{1}{(2\pi)^{\frac{n}{2}}}\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(\mathbf{x}) e^{-i\boldsymbol{\omega}\cdot\mathbf{x}}\, d\mathbf{x}$		 $\widehat{f}_3(\boldsymbol{\omega}) \triangleq$

501 $\chi_{[0,1]}(|\mathbf{x}|)\left(1-|\mathbf{x}|^2\right)^{\delta}$ $\dfrac{\Gamma(\delta+1)}{\pi^{\delta}\,|\boldsymbol{\xi}|^{\gamma}} J_{\gamma}(2\pi|\boldsymbol{\xi}|)$ $2^{\delta}\,\dfrac{\Gamma(\delta+1)}{|\boldsymbol{\omega}|^{\gamma}} J_{\gamma}(|\boldsymbol{\omega}|)$ $\dfrac{\Gamma(\delta+1)}{\pi^{\delta}}\left|\dfrac{\boldsymbol{\omega}}{2\pi}\right|^{-\gamma} J_{\gamma}(|\boldsymbol{\omega}|)$ Here, $\gamma = \frac{n}{2} + \delta$.

The function $\chi_{[0,\ 1]}$ is the indicator function of the interval $[0,\ \ 1]$. The function $\Gamma(x)$ is the gamma function. The function $J_{\frac{n}{2}+\delta}$ is a Bessel function of the first kind, with order $\frac{n}{2} + \delta$. Taking $n = 2$ and $\delta = 0$ produces 402.[82]
502 $|\mathbf{x}|^{-\alpha}, \quad 0 < \operatorname{Re}\alpha < n$ $\dfrac{(2\pi)^{\alpha}}{c_{n,\alpha}}|\boldsymbol{\xi}|^{-(n-\alpha)}$ $\dfrac{(2\pi)^{\frac{n}{2}}}{c_{n,\alpha}}|\boldsymbol{\omega}|^{-(n-\alpha)}$ $\dfrac{(2\pi)^{n}}{c_{n,\alpha}}|\boldsymbol{\omega}|^{-(n-\alpha)}$ See Riesz potential, where the constant is given by $c_{n,\alpha} = \pi^{\frac{n}{2}} 2^{\alpha}\Gamma\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\big/\Gamma\left(\frac{n-\alpha}{2}\right).$ The formula also holds for all $\alpha \neq n,\, n+2,\, \ldots$ by analytic continuation, but then the function and its Fourier transforms need to be understood as suitably regularized tempered distributions (see Homogeneous distribution).[note 10]
503 $\dfrac{1}{|\boldsymbol{\sigma}|\,(2\pi)^{\frac{n}{2}}} e^{-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{x}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{-\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{x}}$ $e^{-2\pi^2 \boldsymbol{\xi}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\sigma}\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\xi}}$ $(2\pi)^{-\frac{n}{2}} e^{-\frac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{\omega}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\sigma}\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\omega}}$ $e^{-\frac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{\omega}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\sigma}\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{\mathrm{T}}\boldsymbol{\omega}}$ This is the formula for a multivariate normal distribution normalized to 1 with a mean of 0. Bold variables are vectors or matrices. Following the notation of the aforementioned page, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \boldsymbol{\sigma}\,\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{\mathrm{T}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1} = \boldsymbol{\sigma}^{-\mathrm{T}}\,\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{-1}$
504 $e^{-2\pi\alpha|\mathbf{x}|}$ $\dfrac{c_n \alpha}{\left(\alpha^2 + |\boldsymbol{\xi}|^2\right)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}$ $\dfrac{c_n (2\pi)^{\frac{n+2}{2}}\,\alpha}{\left(4\pi^2\alpha^2 + |\boldsymbol{\omega}|^2\right)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}$ $\dfrac{c_n (2\pi)^{n+1}\alpha}{\left(4\pi^2\alpha^2 + |\boldsymbol{\omega}|^2\right)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}$ Here[83] $c_n = \Gamma\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)\big/\pi^{\frac{n+1}{2}}$, $\operatorname{Re}(\alpha) > 0$
